text: Discourage litigation. Persuade your neighbours to compromise whenever you can. Point out to them how the nominal winner is often a real loser, in fees, expenses, and waste of time. As a peace-maker the lawyer has a superior opportunity of being a good man.
author: Abraham Lincoln
reference: Speeches and Letters of Abraham Lincoln, 1832-1865
locator: Note for Law Lecture. Written about July 1, 1850
